## Objective

Produce bounded, attributable conclusions from approved rules.

## Scope

- Finite rule semantics
- Proof and conflict results
- Freshness and resource limits

## Entry conditions

- RDF projection, restricted backend and shape validation work.

## Exit criteria

- Required type/property entailments and proof chains are executable.
- Unproven, inconsistent, unsupported, stale and incomplete outcomes remain distinct.

## Risks

- Overstating OWL support or deriving trust from incomplete closure would violate the TRD.

## TASK-011 - Implement the approved finite reasoning profile

Implement the selected class/property/equality rule table over approved exact premises and manifested rules, rejecting unsupported axioms.

### Risks

- Maintain a documented subset; do not silently ignore unsupported semantics.

### Acceptance criteria

- Type hierarchy, equivalence, inverse, transitive and symmetric cases derive expected facts, including GeneratedWikiPage as Artifact.
- Drafts, similar labels and unsupported expressivity cannot become approved premises; stable identity is retained.

### Planned verification

- Run positive competency fixtures through the real rule interface.
- Differentially compare supported positive cases against the pinned OWL-RL oracle; reject cases outside the declared profile.

### Risks

- Cyclic proofs and duplicate derivations need bounded canonical representation.

- Each reported conclusion has an inspectable chain of approved premises and rules.
- Inference rebuild/discard changes no canonical assertion, proposal or memory history.

### Planned verification

- Reopen proof chains and verify every edge against exact premises and rules.
- Compare normalized output for repeated fixed inputs and hash protected canonical files.

## TASK-013 - Distinguish unproven and contradictory results

Implement explicit result classification, inconsistency diagnostics and distrust propagation for supported conflict cases.

### Risks

- Do not use closed-world absence as an unstated semantic premise.

### Acceptance criteria

- Absent facts remain unproven unless an explicit constraint applies.
- Inconsistent/contradicted components and reasoning failure cannot be presented as trusted conclusions or authorization.

### Planned verification

- Exercise disjoint types, negative assertions, inconsistent identity and unsupported-rule fixtures.
- Verify SHACL and operational authorization retain their independent rules.

## TASK-014 - Enforce reasoning freshness and reproducibility

Apply closure/proof/resource bounds, cancellation and exact premise invalidation to the reasoning interface.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-012, REQ-014, REQ-033, REQ-040 |
| Design basis | None |
| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology_reasoning.py, SKILLS-depo/ontology/tests/test_reasoning_limits.py |
| Dependencies | TASK-013, TASK-005 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- Do not label a truncated closure complete or silently refresh a frozen solver packet.

### Acceptance criteria

- Changed premises invalidate dependent results; identical pinned inputs produce equivalent conclusions and normalized proofs.
- Bounded/cancelled runs report incomplete status without replacing frozen Task context.

### Planned verification

- Exercise round/triple/proof/time/memory limits through the actual interface.
- Change an approved premise after a successful run and verify rejection of its old result.
